newsitem.title: FRANCE: Fewer immigrants becoming French citizens.
newsitem.headline: Fewer immigrants becoming French citizens.

text.p: The number of people acquiring French citizenship in 1995 was 27 percent lower than the figure for the previous year, the Justice Ministry said on Friday.
The 92,140 individuals to become citizens represented a "return to normal" from a peak of 126,337 recorded for 1994, the ministry said.
It added that 51 percent of the 1995 total were from a European state and 46 percent were from northern Africa.

Immigration and the right to citizenship have become highly controversial issues in France. Unemployment is at a record 12.7 percent and the far-right anti-immigrant National Front has gained strength in by-elections.
The National Assembly has approved and sent to the Senate a measure that would further tighten France's already tough laws against immigration.
